brief: Goldman one-delta desk head Rich Privorotsky argues yesterday broke the usual pattern, because the US escalated around Hormuz during the US cash session while crude was already rising, rather than overnight. Brent is at $95 and markets price a 66% chance of a September hike. The desk chain runs energy to rates: Middle East and Russian refinery capacity is damaged, diesel, gasoil, heating oil and European gas have all broken out, TTF is through 70 euros per MWh and above the 2022 print, so the US 10-year at 4.80% gets no relief until energy does. Amanda Ross reiterates the desk trade as inverse heating oil versus the 10-year and reports US strikes on about 100 targets including two Iranian tankers. George Cole's overlay is that the sell-off is fundamental rather than fragile because rates vol has not broken higher, while Goldman forecasts still carry 10-year yields 30 to 40bp lower if the driver goes away. A separate section reports Dell's AI server outlook of $74 billion for F2027 as capex inflation sitting next to diesel inflation.
